title: Study for Automatic Detection of Frequent Nursing-Sensitive Events in Intensive Care Unit Patients
summary:
Patients receiving intensive care are at increased risk of adverse events due to the severity of their illnesses. These include pressure injuries, delirium, and catheter-associated infections. Some of these events can be influenced or prevented through appropriate nursing care.
The aim of the SAiFE-ICU study is to systematically identify nursing-sensitive adverse events from electronic health records. In addition, an automated detection algorithm will be developed that can be applied to large patient populations and datasets. Comparing automated detection with manual chart review may provide valuable insights into factors affecting patient safety and the effectiveness of complex nursing interventions.
conditions: The study investigates nursing-sensitive adverse events among critically ill patients treated in ICUs and IMCs. These include healthcare-associated infections, delirium, pressure injuries, the use of physical restraints and malnutrition or undernutrition.

interventions.name:
Data collection will beginn in September 2026 and will be conducted across four intensive care units (ICUs) and one intermediate care unit (IMC) at a university hospital. The observation period spans 12 months, from June 2026 to May 2027.

Exclusion criteria:
